Under the explicit theta-dependent threshold this forces total quasi-norm at least 2m; otherwise l1 mass already gives (2-delta)m. Opposite unit blocks attain 2m for every tail. This holds for complex and infinite summable tail vectors. Explicit delta_m tends to zero and obeys the threshold. Finite diagnostic checker passes 2015 assertions; the infinite limit follows analytically.

originality.rationale: Originality is supported by a statement-level comparison. Berná explicitly proves only m<=q_theta(1_A)<=2m in Remark 6.1. value.rationale: Berná introduced the tail gauge q_theta specifically to exhibit a failure of quasi-norm recovery, but left a factor-two gap m<=q_theta(1_A)<=2m. The new sharp asymptotic identifies which endpoint governs the actual best tail cancellations, with an effective bound and an exact asymptotic coefficient for the discrepancy ||1_A||_theta/q_theta(1_A)~(theta/2)log m. This is a natural invariant of the source space and clarifies the interaction of tail approximation and the bidual gauge; it is not a random finite slice. No broad general theorem is claimed.
